Meetings are broadcast live on Glendale TV, viewable on Spectrum Cable, channel 6, and AT&T U-
verse, channel 99. Meetings are also streamed live in high definition (HD) on the city's webpage,
glendaleca.gov/live, on YouTube.com/myglendale, and on Apple TV, Roku, and Amazon Fire
devices using a free app called Screenweave and choosing “Glendale TV” from the menu. Meetings
are also archived on the City Website for viewing anytime at glendaleca.gov/agendas. Call (818)
548-4013 for program schedules. DVDs of the proceedings are available for purchase in the City
Clerk's Office. For public comments and questions during the meeting, call (818) 937-8100. Public
comments on a specific agenda item will be taken when that agenda item is discussed. If you have
any question about matters on the agenda, or requests for assistance, please contact the City Clerk
at (818) 548-2090 during regular business hours.
  PLEASE TURN OFF CELLULAR PHONES WHILE INSIDE THE MEETING LOCATION
In compliance with the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) of 1990, auxiliary hearing aids, sign
language translation, and Braille transcripts are available upon request. Assisted listening devices
are available same-day upon request. At least 48 hours (or two business days) notice is required for
requests regarding sign language translation and Braille transcription services. All documents
related to open session items on this agenda that are received less than 72 hours prior to this
meeting, and are public records, will be available for review in the Office of the City Clerk, 613 E.
Broadway, RM 110, Glendale, CA 91206.
Translation services are provided for meetings through the use of bilingual staff for speakers who
wish to utilize the service as available. Speakers should state their request by contacting the City
Clerk’s office at (818) 548-2090, at least 24 hours prior to the scheduled meeting. Please specify
the language for which you require translation. The exclusive use of City provided interpreters is not
required and persons are welcome to use their own interpreter or speak in their native language.

 CITY COUNCIL/STAFF COMMENTS  |
 Councilmembers sent their condolences on the passing of Councilmember Najarian’s father,
 Vartkes Najarian, M.D. and the meeting was adjourned in his memory.

 Councilmember Kassakhian attended several events this weekend with his colleagues. He
 had the honor of attending and speaking at the Sustainable Gardens Tour that happened
 across LA County. One of the facilities featured at the tour was Benjamin Franklin Elementary
 School in Glendale which is planted with native flowers and plants and has become a !ocal
 attraction. He stated that this is something that we should replicate in other parts of the city
 and other school campuses in Glendale. Kassakhian discussed last week’s item, which was
 the demolition of an older home in South Glendale. He indicated that older homes that could
 possibly be historic in the southern part of Glendale are in greater threat of neglect and
 dilapidation compared to other parts of the city which will ultimately result in them becoming
 unsalvageable and demolished. Kassakhian stated that when the timing is right, he will ask
 council to have a discussion on how to set aside funds and incentivize owners to maintain
 older historic homes. Kassakhian also noticed that some newer mixed-use buildings in South.
 Glendale have been vacant for several years. He spoke about providing incentives to artists
 and leasing out these spaces to display art. Asatryan stated her support of Kassakhian’s
. Proposal in wanting to find ways to use the unused spacesin South Glendale and for the city
 to set aside funds to make this happen.

| Councilmember Asatryan attended the 100" Year Anniversary of the Armenian Cinema and
  acknowledged Glendale staff, Glendale Arts, the Armenian Film Society, and Vigen
  Chaldranyan for putting up a wonderful event. In light of Sexual Awareness Month, Asatryan
  announced that if anyone needs from domestic violence, to call the YWCA at 888.999.7511 or
  818.242.4155.  ,  ;

 Mayor Brotman established some guidelines regarding Oral Communication. For action items,
 he will allow one person to cede their time to a speaker. Brotman will not allow speakers to
 cede their time for the three-minute’ or five-minute portion of the Oral Communications. Mayor
 Brotman attended a Cal-Cities Conference i in Sacramento last week. He spoke about a
 presentation made by the Beverly Hills Mayor and Fire Chief on Mobile Integrated Health
 (MIH) Program which is a mobile urgent care program. The MIH Program can reduce the cost
  2
  of EMS responses by creating small and mobile nurse-supported units that can treat non-life-
 threatening cases in the field. The Beverly Hills Fire Department is organizing an MIH
 Program Summit and inviting cities’ fire departments staff to attend. Brotman wondered if the
 City can replicate the MIH Program Summit. He also discussed “Project Roomkey,” which is a
 program funded by the state. Project Roomkey is a coordinated effort to secure old hotel! and
 motel rooms in LA County as temporary shelters for people experiencing homelessness.  He
 stated that Glendale staff are putting in an application to acquire funds from the state and
 getting assistance from other agencies on how to fill out the application. Brotman attended
 the Adelante Latinos Award Ceremony in conjunction with Glendale Unified School District,
 which recognizes and honors high achieving 8"-12" grade students. Lastly, he attended the
 Armenian History Month Celebration at the Glendale Central Library and acknowledged staff
 for a well-attended event.
